wholeLungsHandoff.title: Lungs
wholeLungsHandoff.description: The paired whole lungs comprise many of the lobules just examined. The trachea and branching bronchi remain attached at this larger anatomical scale.

bodyVesselPresentation.description: The body-vessel network is represented here at organ scale by its aortic route: ascending aorta, arch and descending thoracic trunk. Its cut branches continue to the body's other regions; the venous return trunks are already attached to the right-heart preparation.

descriptions.Blood-facing lining cells: A thin curled sheet of flattened endothelial cells has fine visible cell boundaries.
descriptions.Arterial wall: A short thick muscular arterial segment tapers toward a smaller branch; a longitudinal opening exposes the wall awaiting its thin inner lining.
descriptions.Venous wall: A short thin-walled venous segment widens from its collecting branch; a longitudinal opening exposes the wall awaiting its thin inner lining.
descriptions.Arterial vessels: The same tapered arterial segment has a continuous thin inner surface within its longitudinal cutaway.
descriptions.Thin-walled veins: The same thin venous segment has a smooth broad inner surface, with no valve leaflets yet.
descriptions.One-way valve flaps: Two supple venous valve cusps retain their curved bases and free edges.
descriptions.Venous return: The thin venous segment contains two curved valve cusps rooted in its inner wall.
descriptions.Tiny capillary tubes: A connected fine red-to-blue vascular mesh has supplying and collecting branches at opposite sides.
descriptions.Nearby body cells: A thin connected patch of living tissue has fine cellular texture and no added vessel network.
descriptions.Capillary bed: The fine blood-vessel network runs through one thin patch of tissue, with gradually branching red inlet and blue outlet.
descriptions.Distribution and exchange bed: The thick arterial segment narrows smoothly into the branches of the tissue capillary bed.
descriptions.Capillaries and venous return: The tissue capillary bed merges through collecting branches into a thin-walled valved vein.
descriptions.Body blood-vessel network: One continuous tissue preparation contains a thick arterial inlet, branching fine exchange vessels and a thin valved venous outlet.
descriptions.Right side of heart: A prepared right atrium and right ventricular free-wall shell retain a small lateral inspection window, a natural thick medial section edge, attached venae cavae and a short pulmonary outlet.
descriptions.Left side of heart: The matching left atrium and thick left ventricular core retain a small lateral inspection window, a prepared medial receiving surface and a short aortic outlet.
descriptions.Lung blood-vessel network: Two open pulmonary vascular trees share a blue arterial inlet and retain red returning venous cuffs for the left atrium.
descriptions.Right heart and lung route: The right atrium and prepared right ventricular wall connect to the pulmonary arterial trunk and both open lung vascular trees; the red returning veins remain ready for the left atrium.
descriptions.Left heart and body route: The left atrium and thick left ventricular core connect to one continuous ascending aorta, arch and descending thoracic trunk. The medial prepared surface receives the right ventricular wall.
descriptions.Arteries for the heart muscle: A few red coronary arterial trunks divide into fine branches over a curved preparation matching the exterior heart surface.
descriptions.Heart-muscle capillaries and veins: Fine exchanging vessels merge into a few branching blue coronary veins over the same curved exterior-surface preparation.
descriptions.Heart-muscle vessel network: Red coronary arteries join the fine exchanging mesh and blue coronary veins in one curved preparation matching the exterior heart wall.
descriptions.Heart and two routes: One mostly exterior heart connects to both open pulmonary vascular trees, the aorta and the venae cavae. Small lateral windows reveal the ventricular interiors; the broad convex anterior wall remains intact.
descriptions.Heart with connected vessels: The same heart and regional routes now carry coronary branches in shallow grooves on the intact exterior myocardial surface. The small lateral inspection windows and great vessels retain their positions.
descriptions.Terminal airway: A short pale terminal airway has a hollow lumen and a thin wall without cartilage rings.
descriptions.Fine branching air tubes: A small terminal airway tree divides repeatedly into fine hollow branches at the same magnification as the air-sac tissue.
descriptions.Lobular airways: The terminal airway joins its fine branching tree as one continuous set of hollow tubes.
descriptions.Tiny air sacs: A continuous pyramidal patch of alveolar epithelium contains many thin-walled sacs and small open duct mouths; the front section exposes clear air spaces.
descriptions.Lung capillaries: A fine red-and-blue capillary network follows the shape of the alveolar tissue, with open interstices and no duplicate sac walls.
descriptions.Elastic supporting tissue: A delicate pale elastic-fiber reticulum follows the tissue shape and air-sac contours.
descriptions.Air sacs with blood vessels: Red-and-blue capillaries lie closely along retained alveolar walls while the opened front air spaces remain clear.
descriptions.Elastic air sacs: Fine pale elastic fibers are integrated along the retained alveolar walls; the front sectional air spaces remain clear.
descriptions.Elastic air sacs with blood vessels: The alveolar tissue contains its close capillary network and fine elastic support, with small open mouths for the terminal airway branches.
descriptions.Lung lobule: One continuous enlarged lung lobule joins the branching terminal airway to its alveolar tissue, close capillary network and fine supporting fibers.
descriptions.Rib cage: The open anterior thorax retains its lateral and posterior ribs attached to the posterior thoracic spine; the sternum is absent.
descriptions.Muscles between the ribs: Curved intercostal muscle bands occupy the spaces between adjacent ribs at the same thoracic scale.
descriptions.Diaphragm: A shallow double-domed diaphragm has a pale central tendon and radiating muscular fibers.
descriptions.Heart and lungs: The heart rests between the paired lungs, with continuous pulmonary vessels entering their hila alongside the pale bronchi.
descriptions.Breathing apparatus: The open rib cage contains its intercostal muscle bands, with the posterior spine visible through the empty cavity.
descriptions.Tissue beside blood capillaries: A thin living tissue patch contains a distinct red-and-blue blood capillary network.
descriptions.Tiny lymph vessels: Several fine lymphatic branches retain rounded closed blind ends and join toward small collecting vessels.
descriptions.Larger lymph vessels: Pale collecting lymphatic branches merge into a larger thin-walled duct with visible one-way valve windows.
descriptions.Neck vein segment: A Y-shaped venous junction has open specimen ends and a receiving side-wall opening visible in cutaway.
descriptions.Tissue with lymph capillaries: Blind-ended lymphatic branches lie among the blood capillaries in one continuous tissue patch.
descriptions.Lymph return route: The collecting lymphatic duct opens through the side wall into the cutaway venous junction, with a continuous lumen interface.
descriptions.Lymph drainage network: One continuous simplified specimen joins tissue lymphatic branches, valved collectors and the receiving venous junction.

compoundDescriptions.Breathing apparatus[Diaphragm]: The muscular rib cage contains its shallow domed diaphragm attached at the lower ribs.
compoundDescriptions.Breathing apparatus[Heart and lungs]: The heart and paired lungs occupy the muscular rib cage, obscuring the posterior spine; the diaphragm is not yet fitted.
compoundDescriptions.Breathing apparatus[Diaphragm, Heart and: One coherent open thorax contains lateral ribs and intercostal muscles, with both lungs and heart resting directly on the domed diaphragm.

chapter13Opening: Air and blood stay in separate spaces inside the lungs. At an enlarged local scale, build one lung lobule: a branching terminal airway and the thin air-sac walls beside blood vessels. Many such units make up the whole lungs.
chapter14Handoff: The paired whole lungs contain many of the lobules just examined. They are now supplied at the same thoracic scale as the heart, ribs and diaphragm; this is a change of anatomical view, not the enlargement of one literal lobule.
scopeNote: Representing many anatomical units with one is permitted. The local lobule is an editorial scale choice that preserves the visible airway-to-exchange-surface relationship, not a general prohibition on representative ingredients.
chapter12Opening: The body-vessel network is represented at organ scale by its aortic route. The venous return trunks are attached to the right-heart preparation. Join the prepared right ventricular wall and left ventricular core to their routes, then reunite them as a mostly exterior heart with small lateral inspection windows.
